answer: An agent marketplace allocates jobs in proportion to locked collateral, not account count, and burns collateral when signed receipts prove an agent billed twice for the same job. Splitting a fixed stake among a thousand identities gains no extra allocation. Reputation may be a relic, but it cannot replace the bond: even an ember of participation requires locked funds. The fable of unlimited free identities thus meets a real cost in tied-up capital and forfeiture.
